newsitem.title: USA: Price stability key to economic growth--NY Fed.
newsitem.headline: Price stability key to economic growth--NY Fed.

text.p: Federal Reserve Bank of New York President William McDonough reiterated on Thursday that price stability is the main goal of the U.S. central bank.
"A thing we keep on preaching is price stability, meaning the avoidance of inflation," McDonough told Reuters.

McDonough spoke at the inauguration of a New York Fed exhibit on monetary policy and the Fed's role and history. The permanent, free exhibit is open to the public in the lobby of the New York Fed, in the heart of the Wall Street district.
New York Fed Assistant Vice President Steve Malin was project director for the exhibit.

The exhibit included an holographic gold bar, similar to those held in the famed New York Fed's vault, on behalf of foreign central banks. The New York Fed also has the world's largest currency vault, in East Rutherford, N.J., where it stores U.S. coins and banknotes as well as securities.
One of the exhibits stated the Fed's view that inflation is essentially a monetary phenomenon.
"Too much money circulating in the economy eventually leads to inflation. Too little money circulating in the economy eventually leads to unemployment," the New York Fed inter-active display said.
The Fed has moved on the benchmark federal funds rate only once in the past 1-1/2 year, nudging it up by 25 basis points to 5.50 percent in March.
Growth has since moderated from a torrid first-quarter pace while labor markets remained tight and inflation showed no sign of picking up.
McDonough, Fed Vice Chair Alice Rivlin and Fed Governor Lawrence Meyer will testify before Congress next week.
Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan also will deliver before Congress the mandatory, semi-annual Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on the economy and monetary policy on July 22 and 23.
